source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 4 / line 6 Pension and Annuity Subtraction (PDF p.18-19 Line 4 bullets; p.19-20 Line 6; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 4 and 6), 65 or older; no payer-state limit in 'a pension or annuity' (settlement fact 1); DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 20,000.00 + public pension paid by NY (you) 30,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 32,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 32,250.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 50,000.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 32,250.00. DR 0104AD: Line 4 (primary taxpayer, age 67, 65 or older): taxable pension, annuity and IRA income 30,000.00; limit 24,000.00 minus line 3 0.00 = 24,000.00; subtraction = smaller of 30,000.00 and 24,000.00 = 24,000.00. Line 22 subtotal = 24,000.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 24,000.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 32,250.00 - 24,000.00 = 8,250.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 8,250.00 = 363.00 (the tax table row over 8,200.00 but not over 8,300.00, PDF p.34, gives 363.00; expected keeps the formula figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 363.00. Other state's pension: a New York State and Local Retirement System pension paid to a Colorado resident. Line 4 covers 'the income you earned from a pension or annuity' with no payer limit and the booklet names no state, so it is treated exactly like a Colorado or private pension (projection covers public_pension_other_state); New York's own exemption of its pensions does not carry over to Colorado.
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income at 4.4%; below 50,000 the booklet uses the tax table, which taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds to the dollar.
